questions.question: Containers of hazardous materials must be:

options.text: Secured so they do not move during transport.
A maximum of four feet tall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured so they do not move during transport.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials containers must be secured to prevent them from falling, sliding, or bouncing during transport.

questions.question: In the Hazardous Materials Table, Column 2 lists:
questions.explanation: Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table shows the proper shipping names and descriptions of regulated materials.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle that contains hazardous materials:

options.text: Keep other vehicles away from the pump.

questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials. Someone must always be at the nozzle controlling the fuel flow.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials, you should do all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Do not use hooks or sharp tools when loading hazardous materials. These tools can damage containers or packaging.

questions.question: What shape is a placard for hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These are called placards.

questions.question: When loading or unloading explosive materials, you should:

options.text: Use sharp tools to open packages.

questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before loading or unloading explosives. Never drop, throw, or roll packages with explosives.

questions.question: Who is responsible for identifying the hazard class of materials being shipped?
questions.explanation: The shipper must identify the product ID number, proper shipping name, hazard class, packing group, and correct packaging, labels, marking, and placards.

questions.question: If your vehicle with explosives breaks down, you may warn other drivers with:

options.text: Standing on the road and waving your arms.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, use electric lights or reflective triangles to warn other drivers. Do not use flares with flammable materials, as they could cause a fire.

questions.question: If required, ____ identical placards must be placed on a vehicle.
questions.explanation: When placards are required, place four identical placards on the vehicle—one on the front, one on the back, and one on each side.

questions.question: How must a shipper notify a driver of cargo risks?

options.text: By writing a note on paper
By putting hazard warning labels on packages
By placing orange dots on packages

questions.correctAnswerText: By putting hazard warning labels on packages
questions.explanation: Shippers must alert drivers about hazards using proper shipping papers, hazard labels on packages, emergency response information, and placards.

questions.question: The only way to check tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tire with your hand.
Measuring how tall the tire is.

questions.explanation: Check your tires at the start of each trip and after every stop. A tire pressure gauge is the only correct way to check if your tires have the right amount of air.

questions.question: If a package says "Inhalation Hazard," you must use a ____ placard.
questions.explanation: If a package or its shipping papers say "Inhalation Hazard," display a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard.

questions.question: The only way to check your tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tires to feel how firm they are.

questions.explanation: Check each tire before every trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only way to know if your tires have the correct pressure.

questions.question: A package with liquid containers must show:

options.text: Arrows pointing the correct upright direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows pointing the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Packages with liquids must show arrows pointing the correct upright direction. Always place these packages in the correct position.

questions.question: When loading a tank with flammable liquids:

options.text: Ground the tank before opening the filling hole.
Ground the tank right before opening the filling hole.
Lock the filling hole during loading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ground the tank before opening the filling hole.
questions.explanation: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, turn off the engine unless you need it to run the pump. Ground the tank before opening the filling hole. Keep it grounded until after closing the filling hole.

questions.question: What sign might show that a shipment has hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo comes from a supermarket.
The cargo is in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often carry hazardous materials. Take proper safety steps when transporting hazardous cargo.

questions.question: Placarded vehicles must carry fire extinguishers with a minimum rating of:
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle's engine must have a fire extinguisher rated 10 B:C or higher by Underwriters Laboratories (UL).

questions.question: Emergency response information must include:
questions.explanation: Emergency response information for hazardous materials must describe the fire and explosion risks of those materials.

questions.question: Explosive materials are most often classified as a ____ hazard.
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials include items that can catch fire or explode.

questions.question: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they confirm that the package:

options.text: Was prepared following all the rules.
Was packed at a specific location.
Will be placed on the trailer first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Was prepared following all the rules.
questions.explanation: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they are certifying that the package follows all applicable rules.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous material label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Place the label on a tag that is securely attached to the package.
Attach a scannable QR code to the package instead.
Make the HazMat label smaller so it fits on the package.
Paste the label on the trailer wall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag that is securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials label will not fit on a package, you may place it on a tag that is securely attached to the package.

questions.question: If the letter "G" appears in Column 1 on a shipping paper, what else must be listed?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material
The type of packaging that holds the hazardous material
The date the product was packed

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material
questions.explanation: If the letter "G" for "Generic" is written in Column 1 of a shipping paper, you must also list the technical name of the hazardous material.

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, placards must be:

options.text: Used on all four sides of a vehicle.
Used only by Class A licensed drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Used on all four sides of a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of a vehicle that is transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: When placing a placard, what is required?

options.text: It must be at least three inches away from any other markings.
It can be placed under a ladder if space is tight.
It can be attached to a background of the same color.
It can be placed upside down.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must be at least three inches away from any other markings.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed at least three inches away from other markings, away from ladders or other attachments, on backgrounds of contrasting color, and right-side up with words and numbers level and reading left to right.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees receive training and testing?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials employees must receive training and testing at least once every three years. Drivers must understand the risks of hazardous materials and know how to respond to security threats.

questions.question: How should containers of nitric acid be stacked?

options.text: No more than two containers high.
Loaded on top of other products.

questions.correctAnswerText: No more than two containers high.
questions.explanation: Nitric acid should never be stacked above any other product. Containers of nitric acid may be stacked, but only up to two containers high.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protected by hazardous materials regulations?
questions.explanation: Governments at federal, state, and local levels create regulations to transport hazardous materials safely. These rules protect the driver, people nearby, and the environment.

questions.question: What is the minimum distance a person must stay from a vehicle with Class 3 or Division 2.1 placards while smoking?
questions.explanation: A person cannot smoke within 25 feet of a vehicle placarded for Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (gases). No one may smoke or carry a lit cigar, cigarette, or pipe within 25 feet of any vehicle carrying Class 1 (explosives), Class 4 (flammable solids), or Class 4.2 (spontaneously combustible) materials.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 items should not be placed in a trailer with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Cargo heaters are not always allowed. When transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials, heaters are generally not permitted.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing while transporting chlorine, what must you do?

options.text: Reduce your speed before crossing the tracks.
Proceed without stopping if no warning lights are flashing.
Proceed without stopping if no other vehicles are in sight.

questions.explanation: When transporting any amount of chlorine, you must always stop at a railroad crossing between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest track.
